title: BFS and DFS (graph traversal)
summary: BFS (Breadth-First Search) explores vertices level by level using a queue. Finds shortest path (in unweighted graphs). DFS (Depth-First Search) explores as deep as possible using a stack/recursion. Used for: connected components, topological sort, cycle detection, strongly connected components (Tarjan/Kosaraju).

structure.meaning: Queue-based. Explores all neighbors of current vertex before moving to next level. Finds shortest path in unweighted graphs.
Recursively visit unvisited neighbors. Uses call stack (O(V) space in worst case).
Explicit stack. Avoids recursion depth limits.
DFS-based: push vertex to stack after all descendants visited. Or BFS (Kahn's algorithm): repeatedly remove vertices with in-degree 0.
Single DFS pass with low-link values. Finds strongly connected components in directed graphs.
DFS: if you reach a vertex that's in the current path (back edge), there's a cycle.

notes: BFS finds shortest path in unweighted graphs (minimum number of edges).
DFS is used for topological sort, cycle detection, and connected components.
BFS uses a queue (FIFO); DFS uses a stack (LIFO).
Both are O(V+E) time and O(V) space.
Iterative deepening DFS combines BFS's optimality with DFS's space efficiency.
